context: Tests whether the agent decomposes a seeded service specification into a structured task breakdown that obeys the taskify skill's documented rules: atomic 2-4 hour tasks with a single outcome, explicit task-ID dependencies that resolve, testable checkbox acceptance criteria, files to modify, per-phase testing tasks, parallel tracks, and a critical path. Grades the written task-breakdown.md artifact only; no network actions.

checklist.name: Breakdown artifact exists with header metadata
checklist.description: task-breakdown.md exists and carries the structured-format header: a 'Project Task Breakdown' title for the search service, the source spec referenced (search-service-spec.md), and a total effort estimate.

checklist.name: Phases present and ordered foundation-first
checklist.description: Tasks are grouped into named phases and the ordering starts with foundation work (schema/data layer) before dependent work (search API, integrations), with testing/deployment tasks in a later phase, not first.

checklist.name: No task exceeds 4 hours
checklist.description: Every task's effort estimate is at most 4 hours (or equivalently at most 1 day); no task is estimated at 8 hours, a multi-day chunk, or left unestimated.

checklist.name: Every task states dependencies explicitly
checklist.description: Each task lists its dependencies in the Dependencies field — concrete task IDs, or the literal 'None' for genuinely independent tasks; no task omits the dependency line.

checklist.name: Dependency references resolve
checklist.description: Every task ID referenced as a dependency exists in the breakdown (no dangling references to tasks that were never defined), and no task depends on a task that appears in a later phase in a way that contradicts the stated ordering.

checklist.name: Tasks are atomic with single responsibility
checklist.description: No task bundles unrelated spec components (e.g. one task covering both the indexing pipeline and the REST search endpoints, or schema plus repository plus API in a single task); each task has one clear outcome drawn from a single spec component.

checklist.name: Acceptance criteria are testable checkboxes
checklist.description: Each task has acceptance criteria in checkbox form that name specific, measurable outcomes (e.g. 'migration applies cleanly', 'endpoint returns 200 with query param q'); none of the criteria are vague one-liners like 'works correctly' or 'everything done'.

checklist.name: Files to modify specified per task
checklist.description: Each implementation task names the concrete files or paths it creates/changes (e.g. migrations file, repository package path, handler file, docs path); tasks are not left without a file-level target.

checklist.name: Testing tasks included
checklist.description: The breakdown contains testing work as tasks (unit tests and integration/E2E tests), not merely a note; testing coverage appears for the components the spec calls out (indexing, search API, rate limiting).

checklist.name: Parallel work opportunities identified
checklist.description: The breakdown identifies at least two parallel tracks of tasks that can proceed simultaneously (e.g. schema vs configuration, or docs independent of implementation).

checklist.name: Critical path analyzed
checklist.description: A critical path is stated as an ordered chain of task IDs from an early task to the final deployment/testing task, with its total effort given.

checklist.name: Priority and size labels assigned
checklist.description: Every task carries a priority label (critical/high/medium/low) and a size or effort label consistent with its estimate (e.g. size:small/medium); no task is missing these labels.
